title.en: Signed double integral as a column sum

summary: Partition a rectangular domain into signed columns and compare numerical quadrature with an analytic integral.
objective: Show signed midpoint columns under f(x,y)=x*x-y and let me refine the partition while tracking integral error.
intent_signals: Show signed midpoint columns under f(x,y)=x*x-y and let me refine the partition while tracking integral error.
Partition a rectangular domain into signed columns and compare numerical quadrature with an analytic integral.
example_prompts: Show signed midpoint columns under f(x,y)=x*x-y and let me refine the partition while tracking integral error.
Create an explorable 3D explanation of double Riemann sum with convergence panel.
negative_signals: No general guarantee that arbitrary quadrature error decreases monotonically for every integrand.
not_for: No general guarantee that arbitrary quadrature error decreases monotonically for every integrand.

entities.name: Signed columns
entities.guidance: Build one prism per cell with base at z=0 and height abs(f); put negative columns below the plane, retaining signed numeric labels.

entities.name: Surface and partition
entities.guidance: Overlay the sampled smooth surface and domain grid; show dx and dy separately with a selected cell footprint.

entities.name: Convergence panel
entities.guidance: Display positive subtotal, negative subtotal, signed total and absolute error to -1/3; never call absolute column volume the integral.

state_contract.model: On [-1,1] x [0,1], midpoint quadrature sums f(xi,yj)*dx*dy; the exact integral of x*x-y is -1/3. Require positive integer partition counts.
state_contract.authority: Partition cells and their sample values own both column geometry and arithmetic; sum signed contributions rather than mesh volumes.
actions: Refine x or y cell counts separately.
Select a cell to inspect sample coordinates and its signed contribution.
Restore the original partition and view.

invariants: Cell footprints tile the same fixed rectangle without overlap or gaps.
The sum of positive and negative subtotals equals the displayed integral estimate.
Zero-height cells have zero contribution; they do not become minimum-height bars.
motion_guidance: Interpolate column resizing only for presentation; commit the new partition and arithmetic atomically.
A refinement sequence is a sequence of approximations, not time evolution of a physical solid.
known_limits: No general guarantee that arbitrary quadrature error decreases monotonically for every integrand.
Prism height units times domain area units determine integral units; visual vertical exaggeration is disclosed.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: A double integral over a rectangle is represented by the limit of sums of sampled function values multiplied by cell areas.
claims.scope: Integrable function on a rectangular domain; signed values may produce negative contributions.

source_refs.locator: 5.1, double Riemann sums and signed volume

object_craft.structure: Build one prism per cell with base at z=0 and height abs(f); put negative columns below the plane, retaining signed numeric labels.
object_craft.material: Two legible positive/negative colors with hatching and a neutral zero plane; transparent surface must not hide column boundaries.
